# Car Scenario QC

In the car scenario, we set the speed on every street to 80% of the NACTO recommended speed limit (unless it was already operating below that level as determined by StreetLight data). This should make most car trips longer in duration, although some short trips on local facilities may get faster as the NACTO caps are actually higher than the OSRM defaults for some local streets.

```{python}
import pandas as pd
import geopandas as gpd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from os.path import join, abspath, dirname
import keyring
import numpy as np
import yaml

# This is used to avoid hard-coding directories. 
# To set the directory, use the command prompt or a notebook you don't check in.  run:
# import keyring
# keyring.set_password("msp", "vmt_reduction_dir", <directory>)

# get base path for data
data_dir = keyring.get_password("msp", "vmt_reduction_dir")

with open("input_files.yml") as fls:
    input_files = yaml.safe_load(fls)
```

## Load data

```{python}
baseline = gpd.read_parquet(join(data_dir, "Data_Processed", "geodata", input_files["car"]["baseline"]))
scenario = gpd.read_parquet(join(data_dir, "Data_Processed", "geodata", input_files["car"]["scenario"]))
car_all = baseline.merge(scenario, how="left", on="trip_id", suffixes=("_baseline", "_scenario"))
```

## Plot duration differences

Most should be greater than one.

```{python}
plt.hist((car_all.duration_seconds_scenario - car_all.duration_seconds_baseline) / 60, bins=100)
plt.xlabel("Increase in travel time (minutes)")
```

## Look at the distance for ones that got shorter

These should mostly be short, as local roads are where this can occur. We filter to a decrease of at least 30 seconds to avoid OSRM instabilities when rebuilding the network.

```{python}
decr = car_all[car_all.duration_seconds_scenario < car_all.duration_seconds_baseline - 30]
plt.hist(decr.distance_meters_baseline / 1000, bins=20)
plt.xlabel("Trip distance, baseline, km")
plt.ylabel(f"Number of trips (total={len(decr)})")
```
